title: How Gaithersburg Basements and Kentlands Townhomes Load Your HVAC
headline: I-270 humidity, cool trunks, and why Crown dryer vents pack with lint
description: Gaithersburg, MD mixes split-level basements with Kentlands townhomes on I-270. Learn why ducts sweat, how pollen sticks, and when to clean them from Bethesda.

sections.heading: Gaithersburg is Rockville’s problem, one exit north
paragraphs: Town Center, Kentlands, Lakelands, Crown, and Montgomery Village do not share one floor plan. Most of them share a cool mechanical space and Montgomery County summer humidity. Split-levels put the air handler in a basement. Townhomes put a long dryer vent in a tight closet. Both load the system.
I-270 adds traffic dust. The tree canopy adds pollen. Returns pull both.

sections.heading: The basement air handler is doing two jobs
paragraphs: It cools the house. It also sits in the dampest room. Cold trunks sweat. Dust from the last pollen season is already inside. Together they are what mold needs.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, start with [air duct cleaning in Gaithersburg, MD](/locations/gaithersburg).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Gaithersburg house
listItems: Musty air from basement supplies in July and August.
Gray film on upstairs registers during peak pollen.
A dryer that needs two cycles in Kentlands or Crown.

sections.heading: Bethesda dispatch — not a Kentlands mailbox
paragraphs: Gaithersburg is served from our [Bethesda](/locations/bethesda) office. [Rockville](/locations/rockville) is the next city south.
Book on the [Gaithersburg location page](/locations/gaithersburg). Add [dryer vent cleaning](/dryer-vent-cleaning) if the laundry room is humid.
listItems: Change filters when pollen is heavy.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Why do Gaithersburg basements make air ducts smell musty?
faq.a: Cool metal trunks in a humid basement sweat. Dust and pollen stick to that moisture. The blower then pushes the odor upstairs.
